messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a burst of GPU OOM alerts in us-west-2 around 02:10-02:30 UTC. A few pages slipped through even though the bulk were auto-muted. Noticed the same pod labels but different node pools. :thinking:
chris: I pulled the prometheus scrape around that window. We got a spike in `gpu_memory_used_bytes` across ~6 nodes, but per-node p95 stayed under the SLO. Lots of noise from transient reclaiming.
devon: Can you paste the query? sounds like a cardinality/aggregation choice might be wrong.
chris: Query:```sum by(instance, node_pool) (rate(gpu_memory_used_bytes[1m])) > 0.8 * on(instance) gpu_memory_total_bytes``` It was firing per-instance which caused multiple pages.
alex: Oof — per-instance paging for this alert is too chatty. We should switch to a grouped alert by `node_pool` and add a sustained window (5m) + a rise-in-rate condition. Also add a suppression rule for short-lived reclaim spikes.
maria: Proposed change: group by `region, node_pool` so us-west-2 noise doesn't spill into other regions. Also use `for: 5m` in the alert rule.
chris: Agreed. Also add a `severity` label mapping: severity=page for sustained >10% of nodes in pool, severity=ticket for single node. That keeps pages for real cluster-level problems.
devon: We should be careful with the grouping key — including too many labels increases cardinality. `node_pool` + `region` is fine; drop `az` and pod labels.
alert-bot: Incident created: #INV-20240421-03 - transient gpu oom flurry — auto-muted 4 alerts, paged 2. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INV-20240421-03 :spiral_notepad:
maria: I'm adding a quick fork of the alert rule to the staging prometheus for testing. Putting the snippet here for review:
```yaml
- alert: GPUHighMemoryByPool
  expr: |
    sum by(region, node_pool) (gpu_memory_used_bytes / gpu_memory_total_bytes)
      > 0.75
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
  annotations:
    runbook: https://runbooks/redwood/gpu-memory-pool
```
chris: Add a second rule that promotes to `severity: page` when `sum by(region, node_pool) (gpu_memory_used_bytes / gpu_memory_total_bytes) > 0.9` for 3m OR `count by(node_pool) ( (gpu_instance_ooms_total > 0) ) / count by(node_pool) (gpu_instances_total) > 0.10`
alex: Also recommend a pager quiet window: auto-snooze paging for that pool if we get >=50% of alerts within 2m from the same pool (debounce). Keeps us from paging repeatedly during a single noisy event.
devon: We should update the SLO dashboard to show pool-level error budgets — then we can tie paging thresholds to budget burn. If budget small, be more aggressive with pages; if large, lean to tickets.
maria: Agreed — I'll add a grafana panel: pool burn rate and per-pool paging count. Will set an alert that escalates to page if burn > 30% in 1h.
chris: One more ops detail: add a filter to the alert rule to ignore `reclaimable` states from the metrics exporter (we currently surface ephemeral reclaim and it's noisy).
alex: For rollout: 1) create staged rules in staging prometheus, 2) runbook update + grafana panel, 3) 48h canary in us-west-2 only, 4) global apply.
maria: I'll open a PR with the rule + runbook link. tagging @devon for dashboard changes and @alex for the debounce policy config. :thumbsup:
devon: On it. I'll prototype the dashboard and share a link in the PR.
maria: Thanks everyone — goal is fewer false pages overnight and clearer ticket vs page decision boundaries. Followups in the PR.
